newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-ESPANYOL KNOCK DEPORTIVO OUT OF SPANISH CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ESPANYOL KNOCK DEPORTIVO OUT OF SPANISH CUP.

text.p: Deportivo Coruna stumbled out of the Spanish Cup on Wednesday despite playing most of their fourth round match against an Espanyol side reduced to 10 men.
The goalless draw was enough to give Espanyol the tie on the away goals rule after the 2-2 draw in the first leg.
Celta Vigo and Racing Santander also won through to the quarter-finals alongside holders Atletico Madrid who brushed aside Compostela on Tuesday.
Deportivo started strongly and hit the bar twice in the opening minutes but were unable to break down fierce Espanyol resistance in the second half.
"We played with all the ingredients we had, but they weren't enough," said Deportivo manager John Toshack "We've lacked bite up-front for many weeks."

Athletic Bilbao, winners of the Cup 23 times, went behind to an early goal against Racing Santander who hung on for a 1-1 draw despite being reduced to just nine men. Racing's 1-0 victory in the first leg was enough to take them through.
Celta Vigo were unexpectedly pressurised in the 0-0 draw with second division Lleida, but went through thanks to a late equaliser scored in the 1-1 draw in the first leg.
Cup holders Atletico Madrid beat Compostela 3-2 on Tuesday night, to take their quarter-final berth with a comfortable 5-2 aggregate win.
Real Madrid will have to turn round a 3-2 first leg defeat in Thursday's big clash against arch-rivals Barcelona, while Rayo Vallecano travel to Extremadura after a 2-2 draw last week.
